classification.difficultyReason: Expand the two tangent expressions, form the specified quadratic, then use the prescribed quadratic formula and recognise exact tangent values.

answer.worked:
Using the tangent sum and difference identities:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}&=\frac{3(1-\tan\theta)}{1+\tan\theta}\\(1+\tan\theta)^2&=3(1-\tan\theta)^2\\1+2\tan\theta+\tan^2\theta&=3-6\tan\theta+3\tan^2\theta\\2\tan^2\theta-8\tan\theta+2&=0\\\tan^2\theta-4\tan\theta+1&=0.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence use the quadratic formula to solve the equation for $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{16-4}}{2}\\&=\frac{4\pm2\sqrt3}{2}\\&=2\pm\sqrt3.\end{aligned}$$
For $\tan\theta=2+\sqrt3$, $\theta=\frac{5\pi}{12}$. For $\tan\theta=2-\sqrt3$, $\theta=\frac{\pi}{12}$.
The original equation is undefined at $\theta=\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4$. The tangent substitution also excludes $\theta=\frac\pi2$; substitution into the original equation gives $-1\ne3$, so it is not a solution. Both obtained values satisfy the original equation.
Therefore $\theta=\frac{\pi}{12}$ or $\frac{5\pi}{12}$.
